boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase places and activities in Rapid City for South Dakota Mines students.

cards.title: Walk among the Dinosaur Park sculptures
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Take a daylight loop around the seven cement dinosaur sculptures, read the setting, and pause at the city overlook without climbing on the artwork.
cards.short_summary: A sculpture walk on a ridge above Rapid City.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City identifies Dinosaur Park as a free attraction and describes seven cement dinosaur sculptures on a ridge overlooking Rapid City.
cards.access_notes: Use the city’s posted park rules; the Rapid City code prohibits climbing on or defacing the dinosaur figures.

cards.title: Explore Storybook Island on foot
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Walk the eight-acre storybook setting with friends and focus on the character scenes, bridges, and outdoor paths; donations are optional.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City states that Storybook Island is an admissions-free children’s theme park.
cards.access_notes: Entrance is free; donations may be accepted. Check the park’s seasonal opening information before going.

cards.title: Visit Chapel in the Hills and its grounds
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Take a quiet daytime walk through the chapel grounds and look closely at the Norwegian stave-church construction; keep the visit respectful.
cards.short_summary: A visitor-open chapel with no set admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: Chapel in the Hills says it is open to all visitors and has no set admission fee.
cards.source_title: About the Chapel in the Hills
cards.access_notes: The chapel lists regular May 1–September 30 hours and limited April/October grounds access; donations and purchases are voluntary.

cards.title: Take a slow lap through Art Alley
cards.subtitle: Between 6th and 7th Streets, downtown Rapid City
cards.notes: Walk the alley in daylight, photograph the changing permitted street art, and leave walls and nearby business access unobstructed.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor gallery of changing murals.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City labels Art Alley free and describes it as a community gallery between 6th and 7th Streets.
cards.access_notes: Art Alley is outdoors in downtown Rapid City; visit as a pedestrian and respect active alley traffic.

cards.title: Read the Berlin Wall exhibit at Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Follow the park paths to the two Berlin Wall segments and informational plaques, then continue along Rapid Creek for an easy group walk.
cards.short_summary: A free park walk anchored by Berlin Wall segments.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City lists Memorial Park and its Berlin Wall Exhibit among free attractions and describes two wall segments with informational plaques.
cards.access_notes: Rapid City municipal parks are open 5 a.m.–10 p.m.; alcohol is prohibited in the park system.

cards.title: Do the City of Presidents self-guided walk
cards.subtitle: Downtown Rapid City
cards.notes: Choose a few downtown statues, use the free mobile audio tour if desired, and make a short walking loop around the sidewalks and public corners.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided downtown statue walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City describes the City of Presidents as a free self-guided walking tour and offers a free mobile audio tour.
cards.access_notes: The statues are distributed along downtown streets and sidewalks; the mobile tour is free.

cards.title: Browse the Dahl’s visual art galleries
cards.subtitle: 713 7th Street, Rapid City
cards.notes: Meet in the galleries, compare a few works or exhibits, and save ticketed performances or classes for a separate plan if they interest you.
cards.short_summary: Always-free gallery admission in downtown Rapid City.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dahl Arts Center states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Gallery admission is always free; the site lists Monday–Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Some events may be ticketed.

cards.title: Cool off at the Main Street Square fountains
cards.subtitle: Main Street Square, downtown Rapid City
cards.notes: Use the interactive splash patio during its summer operation, then sit on the turf or look over the surrounding public art before heading out.
cards.short_summary: Free seasonal water play in a downtown square.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City states that Main Street Square’s interactive fountains provide free water fun.
cards.access_notes: This card is for the summer fountains only; skating rentals and individual events can carry separate costs.

cards.title: Walk or bike around Canyon Lake Park
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a lap around the lake or a casual bike ride, and use the open park setting for a picnic or a simple outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A free lakeside park for walking and biking.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City includes Canyon Lake Park in its free activities and describes walking and biking around the lake.
cards.source_title: 33 Fun Free Things To Do In Rapid City And The Black Hills
cards.access_notes: Rapid City municipal parks are open 5 a.m.–10 p.m.; fishing requires the appropriate South Dakota license.

cards.title: Explore exhibits and trails at Outdoor Campus
cards.subtitle: 4130 Adventure Trail, Rapid City
cards.notes: Walk the nature trails, browse the habitat exhibits and aquarium, or register for a free public class when a suitable session is available.
cards.short_summary: State-run exhibits, trails, and free outdoor-skills classes.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks says Outdoor Campus has free educational classes, indoor exhibits, an aquarium, and nature trails for everyday use.
cards.access_notes: Programming is free; verify current hours and register in advance when a class requires registration.
